caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.42 of 2018
lawyer:
Mr Abul Kalam Chowdhilly, Advocate instructed by Mr Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners 
For Respondent Nos.1-2 ------- None represented
parties:
Golam Mursid Shahabuddin being dead his heirs: Ishrat Jahan Lipi and others ------ Petitioners
-Vs-
Abdul Hague and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 11. Mr. Abul Kalam Chowdhury, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits that the High Court Division erred in law in considering that in the civil revision, no process was served on contesting defendant No.1, Golam Mursid Sahabuddin and process was fraudulently suppressed on him and Golam Mursid Sahabuddin died on 19.11.2011 leaving behind the present petitioners, but heirs of defendant No.1 was not fraudulently substituted and the judgment and order of the High Court Division was obtained against the dead person by practicing fraud and as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. He further submits that the judgment and order of the High Court Division is not well founded as original Title Suit No.22 of 2003 was filed for simple declaration that the suit deed was benami deed and defendant No.1 was Benamder of the plaintiff, but the suit for declaration as filed was not maintainable without prayer for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession and thus, the suit was hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, but learned Judge of the Single Judge of the High Court Division failed to consider these legal aspects to the case and thus, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. He further submits that the learned Judge of the Single Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in reversing the judgment of appellate Court below without controverting the findings of the appellate Court below and as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. He further submits that the learned Judge of the Single Judge of the High Court Division erred in law as it misread section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure and decision cited by it. Defendant No.2, GM Sahabuddin filed the appeal against adverse remarks passed by trial Court against his title in case land and as he was aggrieved by some remarks against him, he had the right as per law to file appeal contrary to the finding of the High Court Division and as such, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. He further submits that the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division erred in law as it failed to consider that adverse remark against defendant No.2 passed by trial Court was unwarranted and not based on facts and law and the appellate Court below rightly and legally interfered and modified the judgment of the trial Court and allowed the appeal.
